extracted.intended_audience: experienced trademark practitioners, petitioners (attorneys/agents/private investigators) preparing or evaluating USPTO TMA expungement and reexamination petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and evaluating ex parte expungement and reexamination petitions (nonuse cancellation) under the Trademark Modernization Act (U.S.). Covers evidentiary standards, procedural requirements, common pitfalls, and industry-specific investigation techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case of nonuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions and Director-initiated proceedings must include nonuse evidence establishing a prima facie case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required for both third-party petitions and Director-initiated proceedings; challenged goods/services are canceled if the registrant does not establish use (or, for Sections 44 and 66, excusable nonuse). Build the prima facie case using multiple types and sources of evidence that create inferences of nonuse (past nonuse, bad specimens, fraud relevant to nonuse, current nonuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable investigation required
rubrics_metrics.description: To show a reasonable investigation of nonuse, the petition should contain documentary evidence and an itemized index that 'helps connect the dots' for the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include (1) clear and legible copies of all documentary evidence and an itemized index; (2) multiple sources such as screenshots with URL and access date, state/federal trademark records, registrant-controlled websites, regulatory filings, private investigations, litigation records — a single internet search is not sufficient; (3) specific descriptions for each source about how the information was obtained, how searches were conducted, and what the searches revealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use in commerce' (15 U.S.C. §1127)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bona fide use of the mark in the ordinary course of trade; not made merely to reserve a right in the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For goods: mark placed on the goods, containers, affixed tags/labels, or associated displays; goods are sold or transported in commerce. For services: mark displayed in sale or advertising of the services; services rendered in commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: No use with the goods/services subject to the proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens or evidence showing use with other goods/services in the registration or mockup specimens are insufficient to establish use for the challenged goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for specimens that show use with different goods/services than those in the registration or specimens that are mockups; these can support nonuse findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use must match the identification of goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: The use shown must be use 'with' the goods/services as identified in the registration; a mismatch can support cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: identification covering 'components for air conditioning' does not encompass component parts for evaporative air coolers; use with a different or narrower item may not suffice. Challenge must target the precise goods/services as identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common 'use in commerce' issues (limitations and exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of use do not satisfy 'use in commerce' for purposes of these proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problematic categories include intrastate only use, foreign-commerce-only use, unlawful use, current nonuse only (i.e., not as of the relevant date), and token use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use in the ordinary course of trade / de minimis standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use must be bona fide and not 'sporadic, casual, and nominal'; what qualifies may vary over time as markets and businesses change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De minimis domestic use (sporadic/casual/nominal) can fall below the standard for 'bona fide use in the ordinary course of trade' and support cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement: claim, targets, timing, and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: New claim: the mark has never been used on some or all of the goods or services; not an abandonment claim and does not evaluate intent to commence use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets Section 1, 44, and 66 registrations. Can be filed between 3–10 years post-registration. Focuses on never having been used for listed goods/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination: claim, targets, relevant date, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: New claim: the mark is not in use as of the relevant date (1(a) filing date or for 1(b) the later of the AAU date or expiration of time to file the Statement of Use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets Section 1 registrations. Can be filed within the first 5 years post-registration. Relevant date selection (1(a) vs 1(b)) is critical when assembling evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party petition procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party petitions requesting expungement or reexamination must include nonuse evidence establishing a prima facie case and satisfy filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee is $400 per class. Petitions can be filed anonymously. Petitions cannot be withdrawn once filed. Once instituted, the petitioner is not part of the process (no ongoing role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director‑initiated proceedings: standard and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director can institute expungement or reexamination proceedings on the Director's own initiative without a petition, using the same prima facie standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director-initiated proceedings apply the same evidentiary standard and have proven effective at eliminating deadwood (very high cancellation rate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation result standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenged goods or services are canceled if the registrant does not establish use (or excusable nonuse for Sections 44 and 66).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants carry the burden to establish use or, where applicable, excusable nonuse; otherwise cancellations follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building the prima facie case: use multiple evidence types and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit diverse corroborating evidence that together create inferences of nonuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use categories such as past nonuse, bad specimens, fraud relevant to nonuse, and current nonuse. Avoid relying on a single type of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past nonuse evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the goods/services could not have been provided before the relevant date or that specimens are fraudulent/altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: records showing a restaurant closed before the relevant date; digitally altered specimen revealed via reverse image search or showing stock images used as specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current nonuse evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence showing present lack of use in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: evidence sales are limited to places outside the U.S., registrant statements supporting nonuse in the U.S., reverse image searches for design marks showing no hits. Use screenshots, URLs, access dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other nonuse evidence (mocked‑up/web evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Website content that shows third‑party goods with a superimposed trademark or otherwise mocked-up specimens supports nonuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify website features indicating mockups; collect screenshots with URLs and access dates; corroborate with additional sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering industry‑specific evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Research industry requirements and regulatory or certification records relevant to the registrant's ability to provide the goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check licensing/certification databases and regulatory filings for industries like pharmaceuticals (FDA), finance (SEC, FDIC), dietary supplements (NSF, USP), commodity trading (NFA), and use industry databases (Drugs@FDA) where relevant to show nonuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen farms: definition and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimen farm: an e-commerce website created solely for the purpose of creating specimens; displays hundreds of products with various trademarks but no actual use in commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atypical features include identical product listings across many marks, unrelated products listed together, listings matching descriptions of products under other third-party marks, and many listed marks that correspond to trademark filings made around the same time. Specimen farms and auction sites can produce unreliable specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen farm evidence (atypical website features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators that an e-commerce website is a specimen farm rather than a bona fide commercial site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for identical product listings across marks, a large variety of unrelated products, many goods on the site that match marks filed contemporaneously by the registrant, and other atypical e-commerce characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: False invoices indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs that invoices offered as proof of use may be fabricated or unreliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for identical tracking numbers across multiple invoices and nonexistent addresses on invoices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation evidence labeling and documentation (petition best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and present evidence clearly so the USPTO can follow the investigation and findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an index of evidence; include petitioner name/domicile/email; provide more than one bad specimen when relevant; include industry-specific search evidence and website screenshots; label all exhibits and provide URL and date accessed. Check the USPTO sanctions webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common petitioner pitfalls ('Not that!')
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent mistakes that undermine petitions or slow consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not try to improperly narrow the registrant's identification of goods/services; do not provide testimony without documentary support; do not submit investigator reports without underlying documentation; do not provide only hitlists of online sources; do not challenge an ID (e.g., 'hooded sweatshirts for babies, children') but fail to challenge the broader term (e.g., 'hooded sweatshirts'); do not get the relevant date incorrect; do not provide only current evidence of nonuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on correct relevant date and completeness of challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure petitions focus on the correct relevant date(s) and cover all goods/services challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence specifically pertaining to the relevant date (1(a) or 1(b) as applicable), establish a case of nonuse for all goods/services subject to the petition, and include 'negative evidence' showing absence of use where appropriate.
